subject: Orion POC: end-to-end p95/p99 latency targets and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Wells <simon.wells@orionhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Orion POC: end-to-end p95/p99 latency targets and next steps

Hi Simon / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — useful to walk through Orion's real-time routing and where latency matters most. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to reference: 

Summary of ask
- Primary acceptance criteria: p95 <= 350 ms end-to-end, p99 <= 900 ms end-to-end for typical requests (avg payload ~512 tokens).
- Streaming behavior: initial token latency is critical for live UI; streamed tokens should begin within p95 envelope above.
- Throughput & concurrency: plan below assumes sustained 300 rps peak with bursts to 900 rps for short windows.

Agreed immediate next steps
1) You to share a 24–72 hour traffic sample and any incumbent tail traces (attachment stub helpful).
2) Redwood will propose a short POC: 48h focused test with mirrored traffic to evaluate p95/p99 under your production mix.
3) We'll provide a POC runbook (link) and temporary scoped keys; we need an approved test window and a point of contact for throttling/investigation during the run.

Questions / clarifications
- Can you confirm the percent of requests that use streaming vs non-streaming (ballpark)?
- Any per-tenant routing that would cause request fan-out we should account for?
- Do you have SLOs internal to teams that differ from the product-level targets above?

Attachments: slo-proposal.pdf (proposal with measurement windows and candidate test plans)

Proposed POC windows (we can be flexible): Feb 9–10 (preferred), Feb 14–15 (backup).

If that matches your understanding, Simon, please reply with the traffic sample attachment and confirm a preferred POC window. We'll follow up with the runbook and an onboarding checklist.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: Simon Wells <simon.wells@orionhealth.ai>

Date: Wed, 3 Feb 2027 18:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Orion POC: end-to-end p95/p99 latency targets and next steps

Thanks Marissa — this aligns with what we discussed. I attached two files: traffic-sample-202701.zip (synthetic + production-sampled traces anonymized) and incumbent-results.csv (p95/p99 numbers run against our current provider last week).

Quick context and answers to your questions:
- Streaming ratio: roughly 35% of requests use streaming (real-time assistant); the rest are standard response calls.
- Fan-out: ~8% of requests fan-out to two downstream microservices before returning to the client; fan-out adds non-trivial variance to tail.
- Internal SLOs: product team targets p95 <= 300ms but tolerates higher p99s during batch imports; the customer-facing SLA is the numbers we called out.

A few clarifications we need from Redwood before committing to a POC: 
1) How do you measure end-to-end? Do you include the client-to-edge RTT or only backend processing?
2) For streaming, will Redwood provide per-token arrival timing in the logs we can ingest?
3) Throttling & connection limits: what are default idle/connection settings and how do you handle long-lived streaming connections at scale?

We are generally good for Feb 9–10; procurement will raise the PO separately.

—Simon
Simon Wells

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Orion POC: end-to-end p95/p99 latency targets and next steps

Simon — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. Short answers first, then the proposed lightweight POC plan.

How Redwood measures end-to-end
- Redwood measures end-to-end from our edge ingress (TLS termination at the customer region) to the final token delivered to the client for streaming and final API response for non-streaming. If you want client-to-edge RTT included we can add a client-side beacon in the runbook.

Streaming telemetry
- We can emit per-token arrival timestamps and sequence ids in the POC logs (structured JSON events). We'll share a sample schema in the runbook.

Throttling & connections
- Default: 10k concurrent connections per customer pool with per-connection idle timeout 300s. For long-lived streaming we recommend a keepalive every 60s. We can bump limits for the POC and for a production commit.

Proposed POC (48h mirrored run)
- Phase 1 (4h ramp): mirror production traffic at 10% to Redwood in parallel to your incumbent, validate instrumentation.
- Phase 2 (44h steady): increase to 30–50% traffic mirroring focusing on representative peak periods. We'll capture p95/p99 across all routes and streaming vs non-streaming breakdowns.
- Success criteria: statistical parity w/ incumbent on p95 and p99 within agreed tolerances OR clearly defined trade-offs with mitigations (caching, model variant, batching). 

Logistics / prerequisites
- We need: (a) an API key for a scoped POC project (we'll provide an integration checklist), (b) a short IP allowlist entry for our test agents, and (c) the traffic sample you already attached.
- We'll produce a runbook (link) and a short dashboard for the POC showing rolling p95/p99, token rates, concurrency, and traces.

Attachments: poa-mop.pdf (POC operations checklist)

I'll loop Hannah for the tech run and to schedule a 30m pre-POC alignment call. Suggested times: Feb 8 09:00–11:00 PT or Feb 9 10:00–12:00 PT. Which works for you?

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0127
